title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
description: The French tune 'Ah! vous dirai-je, maman', later set to Jane Taylor's poem and varied by Mozart. Its repeated notes and simple A-B-B-A form make it the ideal first piece for coordinating both hands.

arrangements.label: Beginner
arrangements.notes: The complete tune in C major with single-note melody in a five-finger position and a left hand of whole and half notes on C, F and G.
teachingPoints: RH C position throughout; the only stretch is the 5th finger reaching up to A in bars 2 and 10.
Every bar has only quarter and half notes - count steadily and hold the half notes for their full two beats.
LH: 5th finger on C3, thumb on G3, 2nd finger on F3; change notes exactly on beats 1 and 3.
Learn bars 1-4 hands separately, then bars 5-8 (the 'up above the world' phrase repeats), then join.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: Two statements of the tune: the first over an Alberti-bass left hand in eighths, the second an octave higher with the melody harmonised in thirds and sixths over half-note triads.
teachingPoints: Bars 1-12: LH Alberti bass (root-fifth-third-fifth) - practise it slowly as a loop until it is even, then add the RH.
The bass changes chord every two beats from bar 2 on (C, F, G); name the chord before each change.
Bars 13-24: RH plays the melody on top of thirds and sixths - the top note is the tune, so weight the 5th finger.
Bars 15-16 and 23-24: the lower voice walks down A-G-F-E while the melody descends F-E-D-C; listen for both lines.
LH half-note triads in bars 13-24 use 5-3-1; keep them light so the melody dyads sing.
